text.content:
The NET's police, keepers of the gates and the Blackwall.

Kind: Net security authority, answering to no government
Base: In Night City: the Regional Audit Office on the top four floors of the old Ziggurat tower (#59), and the lease on its sealed sub-basements
Purpose: Guarding the gates between the city nets and the Blackwall around the Old NET; hunting AIs and anyone near the Wall

After the DataKrash of 2022 wrecked the Old NET, NetWatch walled off the wreck. Everything behind the Blackwall stayed there: the dead Old NET, the RABIDs still running in it, and whatever else NetWatch won't talk about. Every rebuilt city built a sealed local net of its own.

Static Night and the Linkup

A week after Static Night in 2047, NetWatch announced it had "reinforced the Blackwall over Night City", with thanks to "local assets". It never mentioned the Flicker. Then it did what it had said for twenty-five years couldn't be done: it began linking the city nets together over the old trunk lines, with protection it had never had before. The first certified trunks out of Night City opened in 2049, and within ten years most of the world's cities were joined into one interconnected NET, every junction guarded by a NetWatch gate. NetWatch calls it the Linkup. In the same years it banned Agents and their VIs worldwide.

NetWatch in 2070

It audits Night Corp's CitiNet every quarter, certifies the hardware the city runs on, and licenses the Black ICE the corps put in their systems. It doesn't care about petty crime. It cares about the gates, the Blackwall, and anything that looks like an AI. Its agents dive from immersion cradles nobody else can buy. When a runner takes an interest in the old trunk lines, NetWatch takes an interest in the runner: most aren't charged with anything, and most aren't seen again. Going near the Blackwall is a crime the city never prosecutes, because NetWatch handles it without a trial.

During the Unification War NetWatch declared the trunks neutral and closed Night City's gates to military traffic, which may be the most useful thing it has ever done for the city.

GM secrets

Lyle Thompson's theory: the Flicker was a mass Soulkiller event, and its dead are what the reinforced Blackwall is made of. Every runner on the Ziggurat network died at once, on the same Old NET lines, under the same daemon, which gave NetWatch a perfect map of where the Old NET touched the world. The coroners wrote "brains cooked from the inside", but the reports he read said the minds were gone, copied out, before the cooking started. He also believes one member of the crew that ended Static Night has a NetWatch connection, because NetWatch has worked around that person for twenty years.

Edgerunner's Handbook p.12; Night City 2070 (The Unification Era), ch.02, 06, 09
